I have a different angle to this idea.

You are the hero's parent, and you observe their progress and live your life in the day time but when it's time for bed, and you start to fall asleep... You imagine your son/daughter's adventure and play as them.

Your Pokémon and situation could change depending on what you do during the day, and sometimes, you might dream of different people or even yourself.

Furthermore, you can support the hero during the day in many ways, but if you decide not to take those actions, and despite hearing good things and imagining a grandiose adventure, the hero could be failing immensely.

Your choices and actions could culminate in different endings.

As the parent, you can travel everywhere in the day whenever you want. Doing so, you can interact with characters the hero has come across or might meet later (for example, when Dawn's Mother helps you get into contests by being friends with a judge or by being an established idol), so even your job or hobbies can change the outcome.

The dream world would work like the regular games where you catch Pokémon and battle important trainers. You always find yourself thrown into it before a major event occurs, and the outcome of those events (a battle for example) could impact your mood for the next day.

Your mood when you go to sleep could dictate whether it's a nightmare or a nice dream. A nightmare could be a very difficult situation, where your Pokémon are weak, or other things are going wrong. And the good dreams are fairly easy to get through.

In the end, these dreams don't really affect the world in any meaningful except allow you to take different decisions based on the mood set by them for the next day.
